feedback: Written before this candidate races. Race 5 (entityR2A, 606.82) is the best result: the controller change at race 4 geometry gave oval 20 of 20 and s-bend 15 of 20, but slalom still finished 0 of 20 with 1.15 line-loss events and max_error at the 0.06 m limit. Race 1 (302.73) and race 3 (235.88) show that widening the spread to ±0.04 m cut oval finishes and did not fix slalom, so reach is not the limiter. Race 4 (356.98 to 578.99) showed that the y = 0.06 lead lifted oval and s-bend, so the lead should stay where it is. Your seven-sensor layout is the right next test: it adds coverage inside the ±0.03 m reach that already works on oval, which tests signal gaps directly. The Integrator has rescaled the weights so the steering slope per metre is unchanged. The outcome of this candidate is not known yet. Once the race reports: if slalom line loss falls below 1, keep the layout. If slalom still loses the line at 1 or more with max_error at the limit, the geometry is not the limiter on slalom, so hold it and move to gain and speed tuning.
requested_changes: Keep the seven-sensor layout at x = -0.03 to +0.03 (10 mm pitch), 16 mm footprints, y = 0.06, with body, wheels and mass unchanged. Race 5 shows the ±0.03 m reach works on oval, so this is a single density change.

If slalom line loss stays at 1 or more with max_error at 0.06 after the seven-sensor race, hold the geometry. Do not widen the spread (race 3 showed it does not help) or move the lead further (race 4 showed a small oscillation gain only).
If slalom line loss falls below 1 but slalom still does not finish, keep the layout and let the Integrator tune base_speed and kp for completion time, since geometry is then no longer the limiter.
